miniProject.title: Feature pipeline, PCA and clustering with invariant-aware tests
miniProject.brief: Build a train-only feature pipeline, implement PCA and k-means in NumPy with tests that respect sign and label-permutation invariance, then decide from stability and downstream evidence what the components, clusters or anomaly scores do and do not justify.
steps: Build a ColumnTransformer pipeline with imputation plus missingness indicators, scaling and one-hot encoding with handle_unknown, fitted on train only. Add a schema test that fails on unexpected columns, and count unknown categories per batch.
Implement PCA through the SVD of the centered data: components, explained variance ratio, projection and reconstruction. Compare with scikit-learn PCA through sign-invariant quantities.

Implement k-means with k-means++ initialization. Test that inertia never rises across iterations, and compare with KMeans from the same initial centers through the adjusted Rand index, which ignores label order.
Add one more method with its own failure mode: a DBSCAN eps sweep on moons, or a Gaussian mixture with its covariance type and reg_covar stated.

Measure stability: rerun clustering over seeds and bootstrap resamples and report the adjusted Rand distribution. Choose \(k\) from stability and silhouette together, noting silhouette's bias toward convex clusters.
Test downstream value: feed the components or cluster ids to a supervised model on a fixed split and report the paired change.

Fit an anomaly detector on clean data (IsolationForest, or LOF with novelty=True), set the threshold from a stated flag-rate budget, and report the flag rate on a shifted batch with counts and slices.
deliverables: The pipeline package with its fit-state and schema tests.
PCA and k-means implementations with sign- and permutation-invariant tests.
The evidence report: stability distributions, the choice of k, the downstream effect, the anomaly threshold and a closing paragraph on what the results do and do not justify.

checks.name: Deep-ML 17, 19, 341, 259 and 367
checks.note: Public tests. Pass the ones matching your mechanisms after your local tests do; note the sign rule in 19 and the path-length convention the 367 tests require.

rubric.pass: All learned state comes from train only, and a schema test catches unexpected columns.
rubric.strong: Unknown categories are counted per batch with an alert rule, and indicator columns survive get_feature_names_out.

rubric.pass: Components and explained variance match scikit-learn up to sign.
rubric.strong: Tests assert only sign-invariant quantities, and they pass across solvers.

rubric.pass: k-means matches scikit-learn from the same initial centers (adjusted Rand index 1 on separated blobs), and inertia never rises.
rubric.strong: Tests are label-permutation invariant, and the second method's failure mode is shown and explained.

rubric.pass: Stability over seeds and resamples is reported with the chosen \(k\).
rubric.strong: A downstream test shows whether the clusters or components help, and the report states what they do not justify.

rubric.pass: The threshold follows from a stated flag budget on clean data.
rubric.strong: The flag-rate change on the shifted batch is reported with counts and slices before any threshold change.
